text:
Noah: pushed sharded-kv-prefetch + latency-aware-batcher to canary pool B earlier today. Preliminary dashboards look solid: p95 down ~30% for typical chat traffic, p50 ~25% improvement, overall token-cost ~15% lower. big win for short-turn dialogues. :tada:

Noah: short summary of changes:
- sharded KV cache (split by prefix-hash) to reduce lock contention
- background prefetch worker per shard with jittered backoff
- latency-aware batching: batch size tuned based on 95th percentile pending time rather than hitting fixed window

Noah: key config snippet we used:
```
kv_cache:
  shards: 16
  prefetch_enabled: true
  prefetch_workers_per_shard: 1
  prefetch_backoff_ms: [2, 20]
batcher:
  algo: latency_aware
  target_p95_ms: 120
  max_batch_size: 64
```

Lina: awesome. can you paste the benchmark command and a couple of sample numbers?

Noah: benchmark command we ran:
```
./perfbench --model rwin-small --qps 800 --seq 256 --concurrency 32 --profile sharded-prefetch
```
samples:
- baseline p95 240ms -> new p95 168ms (-30%)
- baseline p50 40ms -> new p50 30ms (-25%)
- token-cost 0.0105 -> 0.0089 (-15%)

Carlos: any regressions on very high-concurrency synthetic workloads? last time sharding helped latency but increased memory churn.

Noah: good call. under synthetic extreme concurrency (concurrency 256) we saw memory working-set increase ~12% due to more warmed shards and prefetch inflight. CPU on prefetch workers went up ~8%. we gated prefetch with a per-pool budget flag: `kv.prefetch_budget_pct` default 0.15. when set to 0.05 for high-concurrency pools, memory and CPU stayed within limits and p95 was still down ~20% vs baseline.

Jade: did you add tracing tags so we can slice by shard and prefetch hit/miss?

Noah: yes, spans now include `kv_shard`, `prefetch_hit`, and `batching_policy=latency_aware`. Dashboards under eng-runtime -> sharded-prefetch updated.

perf-bot: canary deploy 1812345600 completed -> enabled sharded-prefetch on 4 nodes (pool B). No increase in 5xx or auth errors observed.

ops-bot: smoke test summary: 1200 requests over 10m, 99.9% responses < 500ms, no memory OOMs.

Lina: what's the rollout plan? any feature flags to flip back quickly?

Noah: rollout plan: promote to prod-canary at 06:00 UTC tomorrow if no new regressions. rollback steps: set `kv.prefetch_enabled=false` and `batcher.algo=windowed` then restart pool (automated via rollout playbook, ~7min). ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-12999

Carlos: please add a note in the runtime tuning doc about the `kv.prefetch_budget_pct` knob and recommended ranges for different concurrency tiers. I'll review the playbook after your doc update.

Noah: will do. adding a short perf note and a sample prometheus query for shard hit rate in the ticket now.

Lina: huge thanks, team. nice latency/cost win and good mitigation for high-concurrency cases. :clap:

Noah: thanks everyone  -- will follow up with the formal perf writeup later today.
